148	def _docx_paragraph(paragraph) -> str:
149	    pieces = []  # (text, crossed out?)
150	
151	    def walk(node, deleted):
152	        for child in node:
153	            if child.tag == f"{_W}r":
154	                text = "".join(_docx_run_piece(part) for part in child)
155	                pieces.append((text, deleted or _docx_run_is_struck(child)))
156	            elif child.tag in (f"{_W}del", f"{_W}moveFrom"):
157	                walk(child, True)  # a tracked deletion shows as crossed out in Word
158	            else:
159	                walk(child, deleted)
160	
161	    walk(paragraph, False)
162	    out = []
163	    for struck, group in itertools.groupby(pieces, key=lambda piece: piece[1]):
164	        text = "".join(piece[0] for piece in group)
165	        out.append(_strike(text.strip()) if struck and text.strip() else text)
166	    return " ".join("".join(out).split())

169	def _docx_run_piece(part) -> str:
170	    if part.tag in (f"{_W}t", f"{_W}delText"):
171	        return part.text or ""
172	    if part.tag in (f"{_W}tab", f"{_W}br"):
173	        return " "
174	    return ""

178	    for tag in ("strike", "dstrike"):
179	        mark = run.find(f"{_W}rPr/{_W}{tag}")
180	        if mark is not None and mark.get(f"{_W}val") not in ("0", "false"):
181	            return True
182	    return False

189	    """Return (text, page count). The text is None when a page is a scan and needs a model."""
190	    reader = PdfReader(io.BytesIO(data))
191	    if reader.is_encrypted:
192	        try:
193	            opened = reader.decrypt("")  # some PDFs are "protected" with an empty password
194	        except Exception:
195	            opened = 0
196	        if not opened:
197	            raise Unreadable("PDF is password-protected")
198	    pages = []
199	    for page in reader.pages:
200	        text = _pdf_page_text(page)
201	        if len(text) < MIN_PAGE_TEXT and _pdf_page_has_image(page):
202	            return None, len(reader.pages)
203	        pages.append(text)
204	    out = [f"--- page {number} ---\n{text}" for number, text in enumerate(pages, 1) if text]
205	    try:
206	        fields = {name: field.get("/V") for name, field in (reader.get_fields() or {}).items()}
207	    except Exception:  # a broken form dictionary must not cost us the page text
208	        fields = {}
209	    filled = [f"{name}: {value}" for name, value in fields.items() if value not in (None, "")]
210	    if filled:  # a fillable form keeps its answers in fields, not in the page text
211	        out.append("--- form fields ---\n" + "\n".join(filled))
212	    return "\n".join(out), len(reader.pages)

216	    """Layout mode keeps a table row on one line; the gaps between columns become " | "."""

218	        text = page.extract_text(extraction_mode="layout")
219	    except Exception:
220	        text = page.extract_text()
221	    lines = (re.sub(r" {2,}", " | ", line.strip()) for line in (text or "").splitlines())

def __init__(
        self,
        provider: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        cache: ResponseCache | None = None,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        effort: str = "low",
    ):
        name = provider or os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_PROVIDER") or DEFAULT_PROVIDER
        if name not in PROVIDERS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown LLM provider {name!r}; choose one of {sorted(PROVIDERS)}")
        self.provider = PROVIDERS[name](api_key=api_key)
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_MODEL") or self.provider.default_model
        self.effort = effort
        self.cache = cache or ResponseCache()
        # One record per complete() call, cached or live. The cost report is built from this.
        self.calls: list[dict] = []

    def complete(self, *, task: str, label: str, instructions: str, content: list[dict], schema: dict) -> dict:
        """Return the model's JSON answer for this request. `label` is the email id, for the ledger."""
        request = self.provider.build_request(
            model=self.model, task=task, instructions=instructions, parts=content, schema=schema, effort=self.effort
        )
        key = request_key({"provider": self.provider.name, "request": request})
        entry = self.cache.get(key)
        from_cache = entry is not None
        if not from_cache:
            entry = {"task": task, "label": label, "provider": self.provider.name, **self.provider.call(request)}
            self.cache.put(key, entry)
        self.calls.append(
            {
                "label": label,
                "task": task,
                "provider": entry["provider"],
                "model": entry["model"],
                "from_cache": from_cache,
                "usage": entry["usage"],
                "cost_usd": cost_usd(entry["model"], entry["usage"]),
            }
        )
        return entry["output"]

17	class MimeParser:
18	    """Parse every .eml in a directory. One bad email never stops the others."""
19	
20	    def __init__(self, files_dir: Path | None = None, extractor: AttachmentExtractor | None = None):
21	        # Attachment bytes are written under files_dir/<email id>/<filename>.
22	        # With an extractor and no files_dir, a temporary directory is used and removed afterwards.
23	        # With neither, only attachment metadata is returned and nothing is written.
24	        self.extractor = extractor
25	        self._temp_dir = None
26	        if files_dir is None and extractor is not None:
27	            self._temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rfq_attachments_")
28	            files_dir = self._temp_dir.name
29	        self.files_dir = Path(files_dir) if files_dir else None
30	
31	    def parse_file(self, path: Path) -> dict:
32	        """Return one email as a dict. `error` is None unless the email could not be read.
33	
34	        With an extractor, each attachment gains an `extraction` dict (see attachments/extractor.py).
35	        """
36	        path = Path(path)
37	        try:
38	            email = {**eml_to_json(path, self.files_dir), "error": None}
39	        except Exception as exc:  # a broken .eml is recorded, not raised
40	            return {
41	                "id": path.stem,
42	                "headers": {},
43	                "text": None,
44	                "html": None,
45	                "attachments": [],
46	                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
47	            }
48	        if self.extractor is not None:
49	            for attachment in email["attachments"]:
50	                attachment["extraction"] = self._extract(email["id"], attachment)
51	        return email
52	
53	    def _extract(self, email_id: str, attachment: dict) -> dict:
54	        try:
55	            data = Path(attachment["path"]).read_bytes()
56	        except OSError as exc:
57	            return unreadable(attachment["filename"], f"attachment bytes could not be read ({type(exc).__name__})")
58	        return self.extractor.extract(
59	            label=email_id, filename=attachment["filename"], mime=attachment["mime"], data=data
60	        )
61	
62	    def parse_dir(self, emails_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
63	        """Return every .eml in the directory, keyed by filename stem, in name order."""
64	        return {p.stem: self.parse_file(p) for p in sorted(Path(emails_dir).glob("*.eml"))}

148	def _docx_paragraph(paragraph) -> str:
149	    pieces = []  # (text, crossed out?)

151	    def walk(node, deleted):
152	        for child in node:
153	            if child.tag == f"{_W}r":
154	                text = "".join(_docx_run_piece(part) for part in child)
155	                pieces.append((text, deleted or _docx_run_is_struck(child)))

158	            else:
159	                walk(child, deleted)

161	    walk(paragraph, False)
162	    out = []
163	    for struck, group in itertools.groupby(pieces, key=lambda piece: piece[1]):
164	        text = "".join(piece[0] for piece in group)

import json, re, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, r"E:\candidate-package\candidate-package")
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
from pathlib import Path
from rfq_parser.attachments import AttachmentExtractor
from rfq_parser.llm import LLMClient, LLMUnavailable, read_email
from rfq_parser.mime_parser import MimeParser
from rfq_parser.render import render_email

EMAILS = Path("data/dev/emails")
KEY = json.loads(Path("data/dev/answer_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["emails"]
def safe(text): return re.sub(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+", "sk-***", str(text))[:300]
def norm(s): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9#/&]+", "", s.lower())
def mention_ok(desc, phrase): return any(norm(alt) in norm(desc) for alt in phrase.split("|"))

llm = LLMClient()
parser = MimeParser(extractor=AttachmentExtractor(llm))
FULL = "E005"
for eid in ("E005", "E001", "E004", "E006", "E010", "E011", "E017", "E020", "E022", "E023"):
    email = parser.parse_file(EMAILS / f"{eid}.eml")
    view = render_email(email)
    t = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = read_email(llm, label=eid, email_text=view)
    except LLMUnavailable as exc:
        print(f"{eid}: FAILED {exc} | cause: {safe(exc.__cause__)}"); continue
    want = KEY[eid]; got_lines, want_lines = out["line_items"], want["line_items"]
    qty_ok = len(got_lines) == len(want_lines) and all(g["qty"] == w["qty"] for g, w in zip(got_lines, want_lines))
    ctx_bad = []
    if len(got_lines) == len(want_lines):
        for g, w in zip(got_lines, want_lines):
            miss = [p for p in w["must_mention"] if not mention_ok(g["description"], p)]
            extra = [p for p in w["must_not_mention"] if mention_ok(g["description"], p)]
            if miss or extra: ctx_bad.append((w["id"], miss, extra))
    print(f"{eid}: class {out['classification']}{'' if out['classification']==want['classification'] else ' (WANT '+want['classification']+')'}"
          f" | lines {len(got_lines)}/{len(want_lines)} | qty match={qty_ok} | review {out['needs_review']}/{want['needs_review']}"
          f" | context problems={len(ctx_bad)} | {time.perf_counter()-t:.0f}s")

End-to-end path works: parse, read attachments, build model input, model answer. Tested live on 10 dev emails with your Anthropic key: 10/10 classes right, 10/10 line counts right, both review flags right.

**Security, read this first.** Your key is now in this session's log in three places: your message and my two test commands. The brief makes you hand in these logs. Before you submit, search the logs for `sk-ant-` and redact it, and revoke the key once testing is done. I did not write the key to any file.

## Example: E005

Text sent to the model (hidden sheet shortened here):

```
From: Priya Raman <praman@gulfterminals.example>
Subject: RFQ 26-0412 Tank 14

<body>
Hi,
please quote attached, thanks.
</body>

<attachment filename="Tank14_Piping_RevB.xlsx">
[sheet "Rev B"]
ALL FITTINGS BW SCH 40 A234 WPB UNLESS NOTED
ITEM | QTY | UOM | SIZE | DESCRIPTION
90 ELBOWS
1 | 12 | EA | 6" | 90 LR elbow
...
6 | 2 | EA | 6" x 4" | Reducer, concentric, SCH 80
...
 | TOTAL QTY | 35

[sheet "Rev A (old)" - HIDDEN SHEET]
1 | 8 | EA | 6" | 90 LR elbow
...
</attachment>
```

Model answer (2 of 8 lines):

```json
{"classification": "rfq", "needs_review": false,
 "line_items": [
  {"raw": "1 | 12 | EA | 6\" | 90 LR elbow",
   "description": "6\" 90 LR elbow, BW SCH 40 A234 WPB",
   "qty": 12, "uom": "EA", "source": "Tank14_Piping_RevB.xlsx"},
  {"raw": "6 | 2 | EA | 6\" x 4\" | Reducer, concentric, SCH 80",
   "description": "6\" x 4\" concentric reducer, BW SCH 80 A234 WPB",
   "qty": 2, "uom": "EA", "source": "Tank14_Piping_RevB.xlsx"}]}
```

It took 8 lines from Rev B, none from the hidden sheet, skipped the total row, and used SCH 80 on line 6.

**Other emails in the sample**
- E001, E004 (revision, 8 lines), E010 (pasted screenshot), E020 (PO by reference), E023 (nameplate photo): all match the key on class, line count and quantity.
- E011: `vendor_quote`, no lines.
- E017 and E022: `needs_review` true with the right reason.
- E006: 44 of 44 lines. My quick check compares by position and the model listed PDF rows before body rows, so quantities are not confirmed there.
- Pictures and scans transcribed correctly, including all 32 rows of the E009 scan and the crossed-out line in E007.

**Changed this turn**
- Fixed a bug the live test found: Anthropic rejected the `uom` schema. Fix is in `rfq_parser/llm/schemas.py`.
- Added `rfq_parser/render.py`: builds the one text the model reads. This step did not exist.
- Installed the `anthropic` SDK in the virtualenv.
- 16 Anthropic answers are now in `llm_cache/`. Spend on your key: about $0.40.

---

# Audit

**What this repo does:** It reads supplier-inbox emails, turns attachments into text, and asks a model what kind of email it is and which items the customer wants. Assumed load: one person running one batch of about 40 emails.

## Must fix

1. **The required command does not exist** (`rfq_parser/`, no `__main__.py`)
   - **What this is:** Graders run `parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json`.
   - **Problem:** `python -m rfq_parser parse ...` fails with `No module named rfq_parser.__main__`. Nothing writes `parsed.json`, links revisions or duplicates, or gives a fallback when the model fails.
   - **Fix:** Add `rfq_parser/__main__.py`: loop over emails, `render_email`, `read_email`, checks, write JSON, with try/except per email.
   - **If we skip it:** The submission scores nothing.

2. **Two attachments with the same name: the first is lost** (`data/eml_to_json.py:L83-85`, `rfq_parser/mime_parser.py:L53-60`)
   - **What this is:** The helper saves attachments to disk by filename, and we read them back.
   - **Problem:** Two files named `list.csv` (10 elbows, 99 gate valves) both came back as `99 | 6in gate valve`.
   - **Fix:** Copy the helper into the package and make it return each attachment's bytes. The temp folder code goes away.
   - **If we skip it:** A customer's list disappears with no flag.

3. **Body text after an inline picture is dropped** (`data/eml_to_json.py:L65`)
   - **What this is:** The helper keeps only the first plain-text part of the body.
   - **Problem:** iPhone mail sends text, picture, text. "Also add 5 ea 2in galv tees." was lost.
   - **Fix:** In the copied helper, join all plain-text body parts.
   - **If we skip it:** Items are missed with no flag.

4. **A scan with one stamped text line is read as a text PDF** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L199-203`)
   - **What this is:** A page counts as a scan only if it has under 20 characters of text.
   - **Problem:** The E009 scan with "Scanned with CamScanner" stamped on each page returned only that line. All 32 items were lost.
   - **Fix:** Treat a page as a scan when it holds a page-sized picture, whatever text it has.
   - **If we skip it:** Phone-scan apps cause lost orders.

5. **A picture inside a forwarded email is never read** (`rfq_parser/attachments/extractor.py:L141`)
   - **What this is:** An attached email is unpacked by different code than a top-level email.
   - **Problem:** The same message gives `image001.png` and `bom.csv` at top level, but only `bom.csv` when attached.
   - **Fix:** Use the copied helper for attached emails too. One walker, less code.
   - **If we skip it:** A pasted list in a forwarded email is lost.

## Should fix

6. **A billed answer we cannot use is paid for again on every run** (`rfq_parser/llm/client.py:L60-62`)
   - **What this is:** Only good answers are cached and counted.
   - **Problem:** With an `incomplete` response, run 1 and run 2 both called the provider, and the cost ledger had 0 rows.
   - **Fix:** Cache the failed entry with its token use, record it, then raise.
   - **If we skip it:** A second run makes new calls, and reported cost is too low.

7. **A cache write error throws away a paid answer** (`rfq_parser/llm/client.py:L62`, `rfq_parser/llm/cache.py:L36-40`)
   - **What this is:** The answer is saved to disk right after the call.
   - **Problem:** With an unwritable cache folder the call raised `FileExistsError`, after paying for the answer. Two processes saving the same answer also share one `.tmp` filename.
   - **Fix:** Wrap `cache.put` in try/except `OSError`, and put the process id in the temp name.
   - **If we skip it:** A read-only checkout breaks every model call.

8. **A hung provider stalls the run for hours** (`rfq_parser/llm/openai_provider.py:L78`, `rfq_parser/llm/anthropic_provider.py:L89`)
   - **What this is:** Each call waits 120 seconds and retries 3 times.
   - **Problem:** That is about 8 minutes per call, so about 7 hours for 40 emails.
   - **Fix:** Lower the timeout and retries, and stop calling after 3 failures in a row.
   - **If we skip it:** "Provider down" means the run never ends.

9. **The reason for a provider error is hidden** (`rfq_parser/llm/base.py:L12-15`)
   - **What this is:** Errors are cut down to type and status so a key cannot leak.
   - **Problem:** The live schema error showed only `BadRequestError (status 400)`.
   - **Fix:** Print the provider message to stderr with `sk-...` masked.
   - **If we skip it:** A failing run cannot be debugged.

10. **A Word table inside a table cell is printed twice** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L123-129`)
    - **What this is:** The reader walks every row at any depth.
    - **Problem:** Two nested rows came out once inside the outer cell and once on their own.
    - **Fix:** Use direct children only, and print nested rows once.
    - **If we skip it:** The model may return duplicate lines.

11. **Pictures pasted into Word or Excel files are never read** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L51-69`, `L113-130`)
    - **What this is:** Only the text of these files is read.
    - **Problem:** A document saying "list below" over a pasted screenshot comes back as `ok` with no list.
    - **Fix:** Add a line saying how many embedded pictures were not read, so the model flags it.
    - **If we skip it:** Items are lost with no flag.

12. **A sparse spreadsheet is very slow** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L58`)
    - **What this is:** The reader visits every row up to the last used one.
    - **Problem:** A 4.8 KB file with one cell at row 200,000 took 4.2 seconds. Excel's last row would take about 22 seconds and much memory.
    - **Fix:** Above a row limit, mark the file unreadable.
    - **If we skip it:** One file can stall or kill the run.

13. **A formula with no saved value reads as empty** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L52`)
    - **What this is:** Formulas are read through the value Excel saved.
    - **Problem:** A sheet made by a script with `=A2*2` printed only `6`. The second cell was gone.
    - **Fix:** When the value is missing, show the formula text.
    - **If we skip it:** Quantities go missing on machine-made sheets.

14. **No tests are kept** (repo root)
    - **What this is:** Every check so far ran once in the terminal.
    - **Problem:** Nothing fails if a reader or the cache breaks later.
    - **Fix:** One test file: dev attachments, cache replay with a fake provider, and the cases in 2 to 5.
    - **If we skip it:** Breakage shows up only in grading.

15. **No `.gitignore`** (repo root)
    - **What this is:** Git has no list of files to leave out.
    - **Problem:** `git add -A` stages 18 `.pyc` files.
    - **Fix:** Ignore `__pycache__/`, `*.tmp` and `.venv/`.
    - **If we skip it:** Junk goes into the submission.

## Nice to have

16. **Unused options** (`anthropic_provider.py:L16`, `cache.py:L25`)
    - **What this is:** `AnthropicProvider.key_env` and the `RFQ_LLM_CACHE_DIR` setting.
    - **Problem:** Nothing reads them. `MimeParser(files_dir=...)` joins them after fix 2.
    - **Fix:** Delete them.
    - **If we skip it:** Dead lines to read.

17. **PDF form-field reading has never run on a real form** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L205-211`)
    - **What this is:** Extra code for fillable PDFs.
    - **Problem:** No dev file uses it.
    - **Fix:** Test it on one real fillable PDF, or delete 7 lines.
    - **If we skip it:** Untested code ships.

18. **Type detection copies the whole file twice** (`rfq_parser/attachments/sniff.py:L17`, `L20`)
    - **What this is:** `data.strip()` and `data.lstrip()` run on the full bytes.
    - **Problem:** A 50 MB attachment uses 100 MB more memory.
    - **Fix:** Slice the first kilobyte before stripping.
    - **If we skip it:** Wasted memory on large files.

`Verdict:` Readers and both model tasks work on dev. Build `parse` first (1), then copy the helper into the package, which fixes 2, 3 and 5 together.

`Lean: about -30 lines, -0 dependencies possible.`

`Not checked:` the OpenAI path has never been called live; Python 3.11 (ran on 3.14); 14 dev emails not yet run through the model; quoted-history handling beyond E004 and E020.

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.
4. **Missing test:** risky new logic (a branch, a parser, money, security,
   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.
5. **Speed:** big slowdowns are problems. Small wins (work repeated in a hot
   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.
6. **Lean:** code that should not exist or should be smaller.
   - delete: dead code, unused options, speculative features
   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
   - stdlib / native: the standard library or platform already does it; a
     new dependency for a few lines
   - yagni: abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets
   - merge: near-copies that must change together
   - split: one function doing several unrelated jobs, so it is hard to read
     or test. Split by job, never by line count, and never into helpers that
     exist only to make a function shorter.

## 3. Check before you report

- Every finding needs a concrete case: "this input or situation leads to this
  wrong result". No case, no finding.
- Re-read the lines and confirm: the caller exists, the value can really be
  empty, the code really is unused.
- A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a
  decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
- Propose the smallest fix that works. Prefer fixes that delete code. Never
  add layers, frameworks or config the problem does not need.
- No style taste, no "consider", no vague worries.

## 4. Output

Very simple English: short sentences, everyday words. Explain a technical
term the first time you use it. The reader may never have seen this code.

Start with `What this change does:` in two or three sentences.

Then the findings in three groups, skip empty groups:
- **Must fix:** bug, security, data loss, breaks at the expected load.
- **Should fix:** risky code without a test, real slowness, duplication, a
  function that mixes jobs, code that should not exist.
- **Nice to have:** small speed-ups, shorter forms.

- `Verdict: Ship.` or `Verdict: fix 1 and 3 first.`

- `Not checked:` one line, if something mattered and you could not check it.

on what you checked.

content.text:
**What this change does:** It is the whole uncommitted code base: `rfq_parser/` (email unpacking, attachment readers, model client, prompts) plus `requirements.txt`, `data/__init__.py` and `llm_cache/`. It reads an email, turns attachments into text, builds one text for the model, and gets back the email kind and the items. Assumed load: one person running one batch of about 40 emails.

The audit's findings 1 to 18 are all still open, so I do not repeat them. New findings start at 19.

Live check this turn, on your Anthropic key: E012, E013, E014 and E021 all match the answer key. E021 gave 50 of 50 lines with the right quantity and unit. That makes 14 of 14 dev emails tried so far correct on class and line count.

## Must fix

19. **A pasted picture with no `Content-Disposition` header is dropped** (`data/eml_to_json.py:L62-63`)
    - **What this is:** The helper keeps a part as an attachment only if it is marked `attachment` or `inline`.
    - **Problem:** A picture carrying only a `Content-ID` came back as zero attachments. The model saw `list below / [image: cid:pic1]` and nothing else.
    - **Fix:** In the copied helper (audit fix 2), keep every part that is not body text.
    - **If we skip it:** A pasted list is lost, with no flag.

20. **An empty HTML part hides the plain-text request** (`rfq_parser/render.py:L14`)
    - **What this is:** The body is taken from the HTML part whenever one exists.
    - **Problem:** With HTML `<html><body></body></html>` and plain text "Please quote 10 ea 2in elbows.", the body sent to the model was empty.
    - **Fix:** `body = html_to_text(html) or plain_text`. One line.
    - **If we skip it:** The model sees an empty email and the request is lost.

## Should fix

21. **A huge attachment goes to the model in one request** (`rfq_parser/render.py:L18-20`)
    - **What this is:** All attachment text is joined into one model input, with no size limit.
    - **Problem:** A 300-page text PDF is 866,329 characters, about 217,000 tokens. The answer cannot fit, so the call fails after the input is paid for, and audit finding 6 makes it pay again each run.
    - **Fix:** Above a size limit, skip the model and return `needs_review` with the reason.
    - **If we skip it:** The brief's own 300-page case costs money and fails every run.

22. **Attachments vanish from the model text when no extractor was used** (`rfq_parser/render.py:L19`)
    - **What this is:** Only attachments that were read are shown to the model.
    - **Problem:** An email with `bom.csv`, parsed by `MimeParser()` with no extractor, gave a model text with no mention of `bom.csv`.
    - **Fix:** Remove the filter and print a "not read" block for those attachments.
    - **If we skip it:** One wiring mistake in `parse` becomes lost items, not a review flag.

23. **`llm_cache/` holds only Anthropic answers** (`llm_cache/`, 16 files)
    - **What this is:** The saved answers that let a run replay with no API key.
    - **Problem:** Entries are separate per provider. The graders use OpenAI, so their no-key run finds nothing here and every email fails.
    - **Fix:** Before submitting, delete the folder, run the dev inbox once with the OpenAI key, and commit that.
    - **If we skip it:** The "runs with no key" requirement fails.

24. **Long lists fail on the Anthropic path** (`rfq_parser/llm/anthropic_provider.py:L35`)
    - **What this is:** The answer is capped at 16,000 tokens.
    - **Problem:** E021 used 4,491 tokens for 50 lines, about 90 per line. A 200-line list needs about 18,000 and stops with `max_tokens`.
    - **Fix:** Use `client.messages.stream(...)` with `get_final_message()` and raise the cap to 64,000.
    - **If we skip it:** Only your Anthropic testing is hit. The OpenAI path sets no cap.

## Nice to have

25. **An HTML reply loses its quote marks** (`rfq_parser/attachments/readers.py:L236-283`)
    - **What this is:** Plain-text replies mark old messages with `>`. HTML replies use a `<blockquote>` tag.
    - **Problem:** The converter drops the tag, so quoted lines look like new lines. In one live try the model still answered `status_inquiry` with 0 lines, so no wrong result yet.

The 24-email test showed three issues. None is a misread email: one is a missing prompt rule, two are steps that are not built yet.

## 1. E023: wrong `raw` text

- **The email:** "can you quote 3 of these, same as the one in the pic", with a photo of a valve nameplate.
- **What we returned:** the right valve, quantity 3, right source file. But `raw` held the body sentence.
- **What the key wants:** `raw` = `MODEL: HV-800-FGS`, the text on the nameplate.
- **Why it happened:** the prompt says `raw` is "the line's text as it appears where you found it". Here the item is in the photo and the quantity is in the body, and the prompt does not say which one wins.
- **What it costs:** graders pair our lines with theirs by the words in `raw`. No shared words means no pair, so one correct item counts as one lost line plus one invented line.
- **Fix:** one prompt rule. When a picture or attachment identifies the item and the body only gives the quantity, `raw` is the text from the picture or attachment.

## 2. E008: duplicate email not detected

- **The email:** E008 is a resend of E006. Same sender, one day later, the same PDF byte for byte, the same two gasket lines in the body.
- **What we returned:** all 44 lines again.
- **What the key wants:** `duplicate_of: "E006"` and `line_items: []`. The rule is that the email with the later `Date:` is the duplicate.
- **Why it happened:** the flow reads one email at a time. Spotting a duplicate needs a comparison between emails, and no such step exists.
- **What it costs:** 44 lines that count as invented lines, which is the second-worst failure in the grading, plus a missing link.
- **Fix:** a code step after all emails are read. If two emails have the same sender and the same set of lines, keep the earlier one and empty the later one. It must fire only on identical line sets, because wrongly emptying an email loses a real order.

## 3. E004: `revises` link not set

- **The email:** E004 is a reply that changes E003: one quantity changed, one line dropped, one added.
- **What we returned:** `rfq_revision` with the full 8-line order. That part is correct.
- **What the key wants:** the same, plus `revises: "E003"`.
- **Why it happened:** the model sees one email and does not know the other emails' ids, so it cannot fill this field. Nothing in code fills it either.
- **What it costs:** the `revises` link is scored and we get it wrong.
- **Fix:** a code step. E004's `In-Reply-To` header equals E003's `Message-ID`, so build a map from message id to email id and look it up for every `rfq_revision`. No match means `revises` stays null, which is what the contract asks for when the earlier email is not in the inbox.

These three are separate from the 25 findings in the audit and the review.

input.content:
"""Pre-parser: split an email body into labelled parts before the model reads it.

Parts come back in the order they appear in the body, each with a kind:

    current    what the sender wrote in this message
    quoted     an earlier message quoted below (or inside) a reply
    forwarded  a message that is being passed on

Nothing is dropped: every body line lands in exactly one part. The labels are facts read
from quote marks and header lines. What a part means for the request is the model's call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

# "> text", "> > text": one mark per level of quoting.
_QUOTE_MARKS = re.compile(r"^((?:>\s?)+)")
# "-----Original Message-----", "---------- Forwarded message ---------", "Begin forwarded message:"
_SEPARATOR = re.compile(r"^\s*(-{2,}\s*(original message|forwarded message)\s*-{2,}|begin forwarded message:)\s*$", re.I)
# A header line as mail programs print it above a quoted message: "From: ...", "*Sent:* ..."
_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\*?(from|sent|date|to|cc|subject)\*?:\s*\S", re.I)
_FORWARD_SUBJECT = re.compile(r"^\s*(fw|fwd)\s*:", re.I)


def preparse(body: str, subject: str = "") -> list[dict]:
    """Return the body as a list of {"kind", "intro", "text"} parts.

    `intro` holds the lines that introduce an earlier message ("On ... wrote:", or a
    "From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:" block), or None.
    """
    lines = [_unquote(line) for line in body.splitlines()]
    forward_subject = bool(_FORWARD_SUBJECT.match(subject or ""))
    parts: list[dict] = []
    part = _open(parts, "current", 0)
    base_kind = "current"  # what unquoted text belongs to; changes after an unquoted header block
    first_boundary = True
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        depth, text = lines[i]
        if not text.strip():
            part["lines"].append("")
            i += 1
            continue

        # 1. A separator line or a header block starts an earlier message that runs on from here.
        separator = _SEPARATOR.match(text)
        header_lines = _header_block(lines, i, depth) if not separator else 0
        if separator or header_lines:
            start = i
            if separator:
                i += 1
                while i < len(lines) and not lines[i][1].strip():
                    i += 1
                header_lines = _header_run(lines, i, depth)
            i += header_lines
            explicit_forward = bool(separator) and "forward" in text.lower()
            kind = "forwarded" if explicit_forward or (first_boundary and forward_subject) else "quoted"
            intro = "\n".join(t for _, t in lines[start:i] if t.strip())
            part = _open(parts, kind, depth, intro)
            if depth == 0:
                base_kind = kind
            first_boundary = False
            continue

        # 2. "On <date> <name> wrote:" introduces the quoted lines that follow it.
        attribution = _attribution(lines, i, depth)
        if attribution:
            intro = " ".join(t.strip() for _, t in lines[i : i + attribution])
            part = _open(parts, "quoted", depth + 1, intro)
            first_boundary = False
            i += attribution
            continue

        # 3. A change in quote depth starts a new part: deeper is an older message,
        #    back to no marks is the surrounding message again.
        if depth != part["depth"]:
            part = _open(parts, base_kind if depth == 0 else "quoted", depth)
        part["lines"].append(text)
        i += 1

    out = []
    for part in parts:
        text = "\n".join(part["lines"]).strip("\n")
        if text.strip() or part["intro"]:
            out.append({"kind": part["kind"], "intro": part["intro"], "text": text})
    return out


def _open(parts: list[dict], kind: str, depth: int, intro: str | None = None) -> dict:
    part = {"kind": kind, "depth": depth, "intro": intro, "lines": []}
    parts.append(part)
    return part


def _unquote(line: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Return (quote depth, the line without its quote marks)."""
    marks = _QUOTE_MARKS.match(line)
    if not marks:
        return 0, line
    return marks.group(1).count(">"), line[marks.end() :]

"""Turn a parsed email into the one text the model reads: headers, labelled body parts, attachments."""

from __future__ import annotations

from .attachments.readers import html_to_text
from .preparser import preparse

_HEADERS = (("From", "from"), ("To", "to"), ("Cc", "cc"), ("Date", "date"), ("Subject", "subject"))
_PART_TAGS = {"current": "current_message", "quoted": "quoted_message", "forwarded": "forwarded_message"}


def render_email(email: dict) -> str:
    headers = email["headers"]
    head = "\n".join(f"{label}: {headers[key]}" for label, key in _HEADERS if headers.get(key))
    # The HTML body keeps tables and the place of each pasted picture. Plain text is the
    # fallback, also when the HTML part turns out to be an empty shell.
    body = (html_to_text(email["html"]) if email.get("html") else "") or (email.get("text") or "")
    for attachment in email["attachments"]:  # name pasted pictures by filename, as their blocks do
        if attachment.get("content_id"):
            body = body.replace(f"cid:{attachment['content_id']}", attachment["filename"])
    blocks = [head]
    blocks += [_render_part(part) for part in preparse(body, headers.get("subject") or "")]
    blocks += [_render_attachment(a["extraction"]) for a in email["attachments"] if "extraction" in a]
    return "\n\n".join(blocks)


def _render_part(part: dict) -> str:
    tag = _PART_TAGS[part["kind"]]
    inner = "\n".join(piece for piece in (part["intro"], part["text"]) if piece)
    return f"<{tag}>\n{inner}\n</{tag}>"


def _render_attachment(extraction: dict) -> str:
    name = extraction["filename"]
    if extraction["status"] != "ok":
        return f'<attachment filename="{name}">\n[COULD NOT BE READ: {extraction["note"]}]\n</attachment>'
    lines = []
    if extraction["kind"] == "logo_or_signature":
        lines.append("[a logo or signature graphic, not something the sender attached to be read]")
    elif extraction["method"] == "llm":
        lines.append("[transcription of a picture or scan]")
    if not extraction["legible"]:
        lines.append(f"[the reader was unsure of part of this: {extraction['note']}]")
    if extraction["text"]:
        lines.append(extraction["text"])
    lines += [_render_attachment(child) for child in extraction["children"]]
    return f'<attachment filename="{name}">\n' + "\n".join(lines) + "\n</attachment>"

"""Instructions for the two model tasks.

They state the contract in data/README.md as rules. They hold no example taken from the
dev inbox, because the held-out inbox shares the kinds of email, not the strings.
"""

TRANSCRIBE_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You are transcribing one image or scanned document that arrived on an email to the quote desk \
of an industrial supply distributor (pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting). A \
second reader, who cannot see the picture, will work out what the customer is asking for from \
your transcription alone. Reproduce the text faithfully and in reading order. Do not interpret, \
correct, complete or summarise it.

How to write it down:
- Table: one row per line, cells in column order separated by " | ". Keep the header row. Keep \
a section heading row on its own line. Keep form fields above or below the table as \
"Field: value" lines.
- More than one page: start each page with a line "--- page N ---".
- Handwriting: one written line per line, as written. Keep ditto marks as ditto marks; do not \
replace them with what they stand for.
- Struck-through or crossed-out text: keep it, wrapped as ~~text~~. The second reader must know \
it was crossed out.
- Sizes, fractions, quantities and part numbers: character for character. These are the tokens \
a wrong quote is made of.
- A token you cannot read with confidence: write your best reading followed by [?].

Fields to return:
- kind: "document" when the picture carries content someone meant us to read (a list, table, \
form, screenshot, nameplate, label); "logo_or_signature" for a company logo, signature graphic \
or other decoration; "other" for anything else.
- legible: false when any token that identifies an item, a size or a quantity is marked [?], or \
when part of the content is cut off, blurred or missing.
- note: one sentence on what could not be read, or null.
- text: the transcription. For a logo, the words in the logo.
"""

separated by " | ". Do not tidy, expand or correct it.

description: the item, self-contained, as a rep would type it into a quote. Use the line's own \

"""Turn a parsed email into the one text the model reads: headers, labelled body parts, attachments."""

from __future__ import annotations

from .attachments.readers import html_to_text
from .preparser import preparse

_HEADERS = (("From", "from"), ("To", "to"), ("Cc", "cc"), ("Date", "date"), ("Subject", "subject"))
_PART_TAGS = {"current": "current_message", "quoted": "quoted_message", "forwarded": "forwarded_message"}


def render_email(email: dict) -> str:
    headers = email["headers"]
    head = "\n".join(f"{label}: {headers[key]}" for label, key in _HEADERS if headers.get(key))
    # The HTML body keeps tables and the place of each pasted picture. Plain text is the
    # fallback, also when the HTML part turns out to be an empty shell.
    body = (html_to_text(email["html"]) if email.get("html") else "") or (email.get("text") or "")
    for attachment in email["attachments"]:  # name pasted pictures by filename, as their blocks do
        if attachment.get("content_id"):
            body = body.replace(f"cid:{attachment['content_id']}", attachment["filename"])
    blocks = [head]
    blocks += [_render_part(part) for part in preparse(body, headers.get("subject") or "")]
    blocks += [_render_attachment(a["extraction"]) for a in email["attachments"] if "extraction" in a]
    return "\n\n".join(blocks)


def _render_part(part: dict) -> str:
    tag = _PART_TAGS[part["kind"]]
    inner = "\n".join(piece for piece in (part["intro"], part["text"]) if piece)
    return f"<{tag}>\n{inner}\n</{tag}>"


def _render_attachment(extraction: dict) -> str:
    name = extraction["filename"]
    if extraction["status"] != "ok":
        return f'<attachment filename="{name}">\n[COULD NOT BE READ: {extraction["note"]}]\n</attachment>'
    lines = []
    if extraction["kind"] == "logo_or_signature":
        lines.append("[a logo or signature graphic, not something the sender attached to be read]")
    elif extraction["method"] == "llm":
        lines.append("[transcription of a picture or scan]")
    if not extraction["legible"]:
        lines.append(f"[the reader was unsure of part of this: {extraction['note']}]")
    if extraction["text"]:
        lines.append(extraction["text"])
    lines += [_render_attachment(child) for child in extraction["children"]]
    return f'<attachment filename="{name}">\n' + "\n".join(lines) + "\n</attachment>"

content.text:
Pre-parser added and wired in. All 24 dev emails re-run through the model: same scores as before, nothing got worse.

**What it does**
- New file `rfq_parser/preparser.py`, function `preparse(body, subject)`.
- It splits the body into parts, in order, each with a label:
  - `current`: what the sender wrote in this email.
  - `quoted`: an earlier message quoted below or inside a reply.
  - `forwarded`: a message being passed on.
- Each earlier message keeps the line or header block that introduced it, for example `On ... wrote:` or `From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:`.
- Nothing is dropped. Every body line lands in exactly one part.

**What it recognises**
- `>` quote marks, any depth, and inline replies between quoted lines.
- `On <date> <name> wrote:`, including when it wraps onto two lines.
- Outlook header blocks with no `>` marks (E012).
- `-----Original Message-----`, `---------- Forwarded message ---------`, `Begin forwarded message:`.
- HTML replies: lines inside `<blockquote>` now get `>` marks, so they are split the same way.
- An Outlook block is labelled `forwarded` when the subject starts with `FW:` or `Fwd:`, otherwise `quoted`.

**Example: E016, as the model now sees it**
```
<current_message>
RFQ desk - Priya at Hollis sent this straight to me. Please quote, she needs it by Friday.
Marcus
</current_message>

<forwarded_message>
-----Original Message-----
From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@hollismech.example>
Sent: Monday, October 19, 2026 8:02 AM
...
</forwarded_message>

<attachment filename="HM-7716_material_list.csv">
...
```

import csv, glob, json, os, re, sys
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
cat = {r["sku"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open("data/catalog.csv", encoding="utf-8"))}
key = json.load(open("data/dev/answer_key.json", encoding="utf-8"))["emails"]
latest = {}
for f in sorted(glob.glob("llm_cache/*.json"), key=os.path.getmtime):
    e = json.load(open(f, encoding="utf-8"))
    if e["task"] == "read_email": latest[e["label"]] = e["output"]
def tokens(raw): return set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9/#.\-]*", raw.lower()))
seen_desc = set()
for eid, want in key.items():
    got = latest.get(eid, {}).get("line_items", [])
    used = set()
    for w in want["line_items"]:
        best, score = None, 0.0
        for i, g in enumerate(got):
            if i in used: continue
            a, b = tokens(g["raw"]), tokens(w["raw"]); s = len(a & b) / max(1, len(a | b))
            if s > score: best, score = i, s
        desc = got[best]["description"] if best is not None else "?"
        if best is not None: used.add(best)
        target = cat[w["sku"]]["description"] if w.get("sku") else "-"
        # collapse the long repetitive runs: show a line only if its (match, shape) is new
        shape = (w["match"], re.sub(r"\d[\d\-/ x.]*\"?", "N", desc), re.sub(r"\d[\d\-/ X.]*\"?", "N", target))
        if shape in seen_desc and w["match"] == "matched": continue
        seen_desc.add(shape)
        print(f"{w['id']:<8} {w['match']:<14} {target:<44} <= {desc}")
print("\nmatch values in key:", sorted({w['match'] for e in key.values() for w in e['line_items']}), "| any candidates:", any(w.get('candidates') for e in key.values() for w in e['line_items']))

"""Read a line's description into the attributes the catalog is keyed on.

    product   which kind of part (may be two when the wording leaves it open, e.g. "elbow")
    size      numbers, e.g. (2.0,) or (6.0, 4.0) or (0.75, "close")
    specs     schedules and pressure ratings the customer stated, in catalog spelling
    material  facts about the material the customer stated ("316", "galv", "a105", ...)
    ends      one set of acceptable catalog end codes per end condition the customer stated
    extras    features the customer stated ("lr", "13cr", "full port", ...)

Only what the customer wrote is recorded. An attribute they did not mention stays empty, and
the matcher treats it as "any".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

_SUBSTITUTIONS = (
    ("″", '"'), ("”", '"'), ("“", '"'), ("′", "'"), ("’", "'"),
    ("½", " 1/2"), ("¼", " 1/4"), ("¾", " 3/4"), ("°", " deg "),
    ("×", " x "), ("–", "-"), ("—", "-"),
)  # fmt: skip


def clean(description: str) -> str:
    """Lower-case text with typographic marks turned into the plain ones the patterns expect."""
    for old, new in _SUBSTITUTIONS:
        description = description.replace(old, new)
    return description.lower()


@dataclass
class Attributes:
    products: tuple = ()
    size: tuple = ()
    specs: frozenset = frozenset()
    material: frozenset = frozenset()
    ends: list = field(default_factory=list)
    extras: frozenset = frozenset()


# --- product ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

_FLANGE_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(?:flanges?|flg|flgs)\b")
_ELBOW_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(?:elbows?|ells?|els?)\b|\b(?:90|45)\s*(?:deg\w*)?\s*(?:lr|sr)\b|\b(?:90|45)'?s\b")

# First match wins, so the specific names come before the words they contain.
_PRODUCTS = (
    ("stud bolt", r"\bstuds?\b"),
    ("hex cap screw", r"cap screws?|\bhcs\b|hex (?:head )?bolts?"),
    ("heavy hex nut", r"heavy hex nuts?|\bhh nuts?|\b2h nuts?"),
    ("channel spring nut", r"spring nuts?|channel nuts?|strut nuts?"),
    ("hex nut", r"hex nuts?"),
    ("threaded rod", r"threaded rod|all[\s-]*thread|\batr\b"),
    ("strut channel", r"\bstrut\b|unistrut"),
    ("pipe clamp", r"pipe clamps?|strut clamps?"),
    ("clevis hanger", r"clevis"),
    ("pipe thread dope", r"thread dope|pipe dope|thread sealant"),
    ("ptfe thread tape", r"thread tape|teflon tape|ptfe tape"),
    ("spiral wound gasket", r"spiral[\s-]*wound|\bspw\b|\bswg\b"),
    ("y-strainer", r"strainers?"),
    ("butterfly valve", r"butterfly|\bbfly\b|\bbfv\b"),
    ("swing check valve", r"swing[\s-]*(?:check|chk)"),
    ("check valve", r"\bcheck\b|\bchk\b"),
    ("ball valve", r"\bball\b"),
    ("gate valve", r"\bgate\b"),
    ("globe valve", r"\bglobe\b"),
    ("weld neck flange", r"weld[\s-]*neck|\bwnrf\b|\brfwn\b"),
    ("slip-on flange", r"slip[\s-]*on|\bsorf\b|\brfso\b"),
    ("blind flange", r"\bblind\b"),
    ("half coupling", r"half[\s-]*(?:couplings?|cplg)"),
    ("coupling", r"couplings?|\bcplgs?\b"),
    ("hex bushing", r"bushings?|\bbush\b"),
    ("street elbow", r"street[\s-]*(?:elbows?|ells?)|\bst\.? ells?\b"),
)
_AFTER_ELBOWS = (
    ("tee", r"\btees?\b"),
    ("union", r"\bunions?\b"),
    ("plug", r"\bplugs?\b"),
    ("cap", r"\bcaps?\b"),
    ("nipple", r"\bnipples?\b|\bnip\b"),
    ("pipe", r"\bpipe\b"),
)
# Parts that share a word with a stocked product but are a different thing.
_NOT_STOCKED = re.compile(r"spectacle|paddle blind|spade|plug valve|needle valve|relief valve|control valve|lap joint")


def _products(text: str) -> tuple:
    if _NOT_STOCKED.search(text):
        return ()
    for name, pattern in _PRODUCTS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            return (name,)
    if _FLANGE_WORD.search(text):  # short codes are only trusted next to the word "flange"
        for name, pattern in (("weld neck flange", r"\bwn\b"), ("slip-on flange", r"\bso\b"), ("blind flange", r"\bbld?\b")):
            if re.search(pattern, text):
                return (name,)
        return ()
    if _ELBOW_WORD.search(text):
        if re.search(r"\b45\b", text):
            return ("45 elbow",)
        if re.search(r"\b90\b", text):
            return ("90 elbow",)
        return ("90 elbow", "45 elbow")  # the angle was not stated: the customer has to say

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from .attributes import CATALOG_MATERIALS, parse_catalog_extra, parse_catalog_size

def load_catalog(path: Path | None = None) -> list[Part]:
    parts = []
    with open(path or DEFAULT_CATALOG, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        for row in csv.DictReader(handle):

                    ends=row["ends"].strip(),
                    extra=row["extra"].strip(),

"""Read a line's description into the attributes the catalog is keyed on.

    product   which kind of part (may be two when the wording leaves it open, e.g. "elbow")
    size      numbers, e.g. (2.0,) or (6.0, 4.0) or (0.75, "close")
    specs     schedules and pressure ratings the customer stated, in catalog spelling
    material  facts about the material the customer stated ("316", "galv", "a105", ...)
    ends      one set of acceptable catalog end codes per end condition the customer stated
    extras    features the customer stated ("lr", "13cr", "full port", ...)

Only what the customer wrote is recorded. An attribute they did not mention stays empty, and
the matcher treats it as "any".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

_SUBSTITUTIONS = (
    ("″", '"'), ("”", '"'), ("“", '"'), ("′", "'"), ("’", "'"),
    ("½", " 1/2"), ("¼", " 1/4"), ("¾", " 3/4"), ("°", " deg "),
    ("×", " x "), ("–", "-"), ("—", "-"),
)  # fmt: skip


def clean(description: str) -> str:
    """Lower-case text with typographic marks turned into the plain ones the patterns expect."""
    for old, new in _SUBSTITUTIONS:
        description = description.replace(old, new)
    return description.lower()


@dataclass
class Attributes:
    products: tuple = ()
    size: tuple = ()
    specs: frozenset = frozenset()
    material: frozenset = frozenset()
    ends: list = field(default_factory=list)
    extras: frozenset = frozenset()


# --- product ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

_FLANGE_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(?:flanges?|flg|flgs)\b")
_ELBOW_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(?:elbows?|ells?|els?)\b|\b(?:90|45)\s*(?:deg\w*)?\s*(?:lr|sr)\b|\b(?:90|45)'?s\b")

# First match wins, so the specific names come before the words they contain.
_PRODUCTS = (
    ("stud bolt", r"\bstuds?\b"),
    ("hex cap screw", r"cap screws?|\bhcs\b|hex (?:head )?bolts?"),
    ("heavy hex nut", r"heavy hex nuts?|\bhh nuts?|\b2h nuts?"),
    ("channel spring nut", r"spring nuts?|channel nuts?|strut nuts?"),
    ("hex nut", r"hex nuts?"),
    ("threaded rod", r"threaded rod|all[\s-]*thread|\batr\b"),
    ("strut channel", r"\bstrut\b|unistrut"),
    ("pipe clamp", r"pipe clamps?|strut clamps?"),
    ("clevis hanger", r"clevis"),
    ("pipe thread dope", r"thread dope|pipe dope|thread sealant"),
    ("ptfe thread tape", r"thread tape|teflon tape|ptfe tape"),
    ("spiral wound gasket", r"spiral[\s-]*wound|\bspw\b|\bswg\b"),
    ("y-strainer", r"strainers?"),
    ("butterfly valve", r"butterfly|\bbfly\b|\bbfv\b"),
    ("swing check valve", r"swing[\s-]*(?:check|chk)"),
    ("check valve", r"\bcheck\b|\bchk\b"),
    ("ball valve", r"\bball\b"),
    ("gate valve", r"\bgate\b"),
    ("globe valve", r"\bglobe\b"),
    ("weld neck flange", r"weld[\s-]*neck|\bwnrf\b|\brfwn\b"),
    ("slip-on flange", r"slip[\s-]*on|\bsorf\b|\brfso\b"),
    ("blind flange", r"\bblind\b"),
    ("half coupling", r"half[\s-]*(?:couplings?|cplg)"),
    ("coupling", r"couplings?|\bcplgs?\b"),
    ("hex bushing", r"bushings?|\bbush\b"),
    ("street elbow", r"street[\s-]*(?:elbows?|ells?)|\bst\.? ells?\b"),
)
_AFTER_ELBOWS = (
    ("tee", r"\btees?\b"),
    ("union", r"\bunions?\b"),
    ("plug", r"\bplugs?\b"),
    ("cap", r"\bcaps?\b"),
    ("nipple", r"\bnipples?\b|\bnip\b"),
    ("pipe", r"\bpipe\b"),
)
# Parts that share a word with a stocked product but are a different thing.
_NOT_STOCKED = re.compile(r"spectacle|paddle blind|spade|plug valve|needle valve|relief valve|control valve|lap joint")


def _products(text: str) -> tuple:
    if _NOT_STOCKED.search(text):
        return ()
    for name, pattern in _PRODUCTS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            return (name,)
    if _FLANGE_WORD.search(text):  # short codes are only trusted next to the word "flange"
        for name, pattern in (("weld neck flange", r"\bwn\b"), ("slip-on flange", r"\bso\b"), ("blind flange", r"\bbld?\b")):
            if re.search(pattern, text):
                return (name,)
        return ()
    if _ELBOW_WORD.search(text):
        if re.search(r"\b45\b", text):
            return ("45 elbow",)
        if re.search(r"\b90\b", text):
            return ("90 elbow",)
        return ("90 elbow", "45 elbow")  # the angle was not stated: the customer has to say
    if re.search(r"\breducers?\b|\b(?:conc|ecc)\.?\s*red\b", text):
        if re.search(r"\becc", text):
            return ("eccentric reducer",)
        if re.search(r"\bconc", text):
            return ("concentric reducer",)
        return ("concentric reducer", "eccentric reducer")
    for name, pattern in _AFTER_ELBOWS:
        if re.search(pattern, text):
            return (name,)
    return ()


# --- size ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Numbers that are not sizes. They are blanked out before sizes are looked for.
_NOT_A_SIZE = (
    r"\b\d+\s*(?:#|lbs?\b|wog\b|cwp\b|psi\b)", r"(?:\bclass|\bcl\.?)\s*\d+", r"#\s*\d+",
    r"\bsch(?:edule)?\.?\s*\d+s?\b", r"\b\d+\s*(?:ga|gauge)\b",
    r"\ba\s?\d{2,3}[a-z]?\b", r"\b(?:tp|wp|f|ss|type)\s?\d{3}l?\b", r"\b(?:304|316|317|321|347|410)l?\b",
    r"\bb7m?\b", r"\bb8m?\b", r"\b2h\b", r"\b8m\b", r"\bgr(?:ade)?\.?\s*\d+\b", r"\b13\s*%?\s*cr\b", r"\bcf8m?\b",
    r"\b(?:90|45)\b(?=\s*(?:deg|d\b|lr\b|sr\b|elbow|ell|el\b|'?s\b))", r"(?:elbows?|ells?)\W{0,3}(?:90|45)\b",
    r"(?:w/|with)\s*\(?\d+\)?\s*(?:heavy\s*)?(?:hex\s*)?nuts?", r"\b\d+\s*(?:heavy\s*)?hex nuts?",
    r"\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:'|ft\b|feet\b|foot\b)", r"\bmodel[:#\s]+\S+", r"\bser(?:ial)?\.?\s*(?:no\.?|#)?[:\s]+\S+",
    r"\bp/?n[:#\s]+\S+", r"\bitem\s*#?\s*\d+", r"\b\d{5,}\b",

_THREAD_PITCH = (re.compile(r'"\s*-\s*\d{1,2}\b(?![/"\d])'), re.compile(r"(?<=\d/\d)-\d{1,2}\b(?![/\d])"))
_DIMENSION = re.compile(
    r'(?<![\w/.#-])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?:[ -](\d+)/(\d+)|/(\d+))?(?![\w#])\s*("|in\b\.?|inch(?:es)?\b)?'
)
_TIMES = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:x|by)\s*$")
_TWO_NUMBER_SIZES = {"stud bolt", "hex cap screw", "nipple"}  # diameter and length
_LARGE_END_FIRST = {"concentric reducer", "eccentric reducer", "hex bushing"}


def _size(text: str, products: tuple) -> tuple:
    text = _THREAD_PITCH[0].sub('"', text)
    text = _THREAD_PITCH[1].sub("", text)
    for pattern in _NOT_A_SIZE:
        text = re.sub(pattern, " ", text)
    found = []  # (value, start, end, has inch mark)
    for m in _DIMENSION.finditer(text):
        whole, numerator, denominator, simple_denominator, mark = m.groups()
        value = float(whole)
        if numerator:
            value += int(numerator) / int(denominator)
        elif simple_denominator:
            value = value / int(simple_denominator)
        found.append((value, m.start(), m.end(), bool(mark)))
    if not found:
        return ()
    product = products[0] if products else ""
    size = None
    for (a, _, a_end, _), (b, b_start, _, _) in zip(found, found[1:]):
        if _TIMES.match(text[a_end:b_start]):  # "6 x 4"
            size = (a, b)
            break
    if size is None and product in _TWO_NUMBER_SIZES and len(found) >= 2:
        size = (found[0][0], found[1][0])
    if size is None:
        marked = [f for f in found if f[3]]
        size = ((marked or found)[0][0],)
    if product == "nipple" and "close" in text:
        size = (size[0], "close")
    if product in _LARGE_END_FIRST and len(size) == 2:
        size = tuple(sorted(size, reverse=True))
    return size


def parse_catalog_size(value: str) -> tuple:
    """The catalog's own size column ("1-1/2", "6 x 4", "3/4 x close") in the same form."""
    out = []
    for piece in value.lower().split(" x "):
        piece = piece.strip()
        if not piece:
            continue
        if piece == "close":
            out.append("close")
            continue
        total = 0.0
        for part in piece.split("-"):
            total += int(part.split("/")[0]) / int(part.split("/")[1]) if "/" in part else float(part)
        out.append(total)
    return tuple(out)


# --- spec, material, ends, extras ---------------------------------------------------------


def _specs(text: str) -> frozenset:
    found = set()
    for pattern in (r"\b(\d{3,4})\s*(?:#|lbs?\b)", r"(?:\bclass|\bcl\.?)\s*(\d{3,4})\b", r"\b(\d{3,4})\s*class\b", r"#\s*(\d{3,4})\b"):

    found.update(f"SCH {n.upper()}" for n in re.findall(r"\bsch(?:edule)?\.?\s*(\d{2,3}s?)\b", text))
    found.update(f"{n} GA" for n in re.findall(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:ga|gauge)\b", text))
    return frozenset(found)


def spec_kind(spec: str) -> str:

    if spec.endswith("#") or spec.endswith("WOG"):

    return "gauge" if spec.endswith("GA") else ""

    ("brass", r"\bbrass\b"), ("cast iron", r"cast iron|\bci\b"), ("wcb", r"\bwcb\b"),
    ("cs", r"carbon steel|\bcs\b|\bc\.s\.|\bcstl\b"), ("b7", r"\bb7\b"), ("b8m", r"\bb8m\b"), ("2h", r"\b2h\b"),
    ("8m", r"\b8m\b"), ("zinc", r"\bzinc\b"), ("gr5", r"\bgr(?:ade)?\.?\s*5\b"), ("graphite", r"graphite|grafoil"),
    ("cf8m", r"\bcf8m?\b"), ("ductile", r"ductile"), ("pvc", r"\bc?pvc\b"), ("copper", r"copper"),
    ("chrome-moly", r"chrome[\s-]?moly|\b(?:p|f|wp)(?:11|22|91)\b"), ("monel", r"monel"), ("hastelloy", r"hastelloy"),
    ("inconel", r"inconel"), ("duplex", r"duplex|\b2205\b|\b2507\b"), ("alloy 20", r"alloy\s*20"),
    ("aluminum", r"alumin"), ("titanium", r"titanium"), ("b7m", r"\bb7m\b"), ("b8", r"\bb8\b"),
    ("other stainless", r"\b(?:317|321|347|410)l?\b"), ("ptfe gasket", r"ptfe gasket|teflon gasket|rubber|neoprene|epdm|viton"),
)  # fmt: skip

CATALOG_MATERIALS = {
    "A105": {"a105", "cs"}, "A106B SMLS": {"a106", "smls", "cs", "black"}, "A53B ERW": {"a53", "erw", "cs", "black"},
    "A53 GALV": {"a53", "galv", "cs"}, "A234 WPB": {"a234", "wpb", "cs"}, "MI BLACK": {"mi", "black"},
    "MI GALV": {"mi", "galv"}, "304 SS": {"304", "ss"}, "316 SS": {"316", "ss"},
    "A182 F304L": {"a182", "304", "304l", "ss"}, "A182 F316L": {"a182", "316", "316l", "ss"},
    "A312 TP304L": {"a312", "304", "304l", "ss"}, "A312 TP316L": {"a312", "316", "316l", "ss"},

    "CAST IRON": {"cast iron"}, "WCB": {"wcb", "a216", "cs"}, "CARBON STEEL": {"cs"}, "GALV": {"galv"},

content.text:
Interpreter is built in `rfq_parser/interpreter/`. On the dev answer key it agrees on 210 of 210 lines: 194 matched with the right SKU, 16 `not_in_catalog`, 0 wrong confident matches.

**Use**
```python
record = Interpreter().interpret(answer)   # answer = what read_email returns
```

**What it does**
- **Shape:** turns the model's answer into the README record: adds `revises` and `duplicate_of` as null, drops `summary`, and applies the contract's rules.
  - A non-request class gets no lines and no review flag.
  - A request with no lines is forced to `needs_review`.
  - A review flag always has a reason.
- **Catalog:** adds `sku`, `match`, `match_reason`, and `candidates` when ambiguous, to every line. It never removes a line.

**How a line is matched**
1. Code reads the description into attributes: product, size, spec, material, ends, feature.
2. Catalog rows with the same product and size are the starting set.
3. Each attribute the customer stated must agree. An attribute they did not state rules nothing out.
4. One row left is `matched`. None is `not_in_catalog`. Several is `ambiguous`.

No model call is used, so it costs nothing and gives the same answer every run.

**Examples of the reason line**
- `one part fits: PIPE 3" SCH 40 A53B ERW T&C`
- `ball valve 2 is stocked, but not with spec 125# (stocked: 1000 WOG, 200 WOG, 600 WOG)`
- `2 stocked parts fit; the customer must choose product (45 elbow, 90 elbow)`, for "elbow" with no angle stated.

**Tests**
- All 24 saved model answers produce records that pass `data/check_format.py` with 0 problems.
- 39 made-up descriptions in wording the dev inbox does not use, for example `3" 150 lb RFWN flange A105`, `4 x 6 conc reducer sch 40 wpb`, `stud bolt 5/8-11 x 3.5 B7`. I read each result and found no wrong one.
- Unstocked things such as `2" PVC ball valve`, `1/2" needle valve` and `safety gloves` come back `not_in_catalog`.

**How far to trust it**
- I wrote the rules after reading the answer key, so 210 of 210 is the best case.
- `ambiguous` never appears in the dev key. That path is tested only on my made-up lines.
- The synonym lists are hand-written. A word they do not know is ignored, which can turn a miss into a match.

**Not done**
- Nothing calls it yet: there is still no `parse` command.
- The check that each line's `raw` exists in the email is not built. That is the one that catches invented lines.
- Duplicates (E008) and `revises` (E004) are unchanged.

content.text:
The pre-parser sees one email at a time, so it cannot decide "duplicate" by itself. What it can do is add a fingerprint to each email, which a later step compares across the inbox.

**What the pre-parser can add per email**
- `sender`: the bare address, lower-cased.
- `date`: the `Date:` header as a real timestamp, so "later" can be decided.
- `message_id`: already there. Two emails with the same `Message-ID` are the same email delivered twice.
- `attachment_hashes`: a hash of each attached file's bytes, leaving out inline logos.
- `item_lines`: the lines of the current message that look like items, with case and spacing normalised.

**What that catches on E006 and E008**
- Same sender.
- Same PDF hash (`6bb112499d`).
- Same two gasket lines in the body.
- The rest of the body differs ("RFQ attached, need it back by Friday" against "Resending in case the first one didn't come through"), so a hash of the whole body would miss it. That is why the fingerprint uses item lines, not the full text.

**Where it goes wrong**
- Two emails with no attachment and no item lines ("same as last time, please") have equal, empty fingerprints. The rule must require at least one attachment hash or one item line.
- A customer who resends with one quantity changed looks almost the same. That is a revision or a new request, not a duplicate. Marking it as a duplicate empties its lines, which is a lost order.

**My recommendation**
- Pre-parser: add the fingerprint fields above.
- Before the model: treat identical `Message-ID` as a duplicate. It is exact, and it saves the model call.
- After the model: decide all other duplicates on identical extracted lines plus same sender. E006 and E008 both give the same 44 lines, so this is exact with no guessing. The later `Date:` becomes the duplicate.

The fingerprint from the pre-parser then serves as a second confirmation, not as the decision.

# --- duplicates ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The later email says it is a repeat.
_RESEND = re.compile(
    r"\bre-?sen[dt]\w*|\bsending (?:this |it )?again\b|\b(?:second|2nd|third|3rd) (?:request|attempt|time)\b"
    r"|did(?:n'?t| not) (?:come|go) through|did you (?:get|receive)",
    re.I,
)
# Words that mean the later email asks for something different, even with no number in it
# ("double all quantities", "drop the valves", "two more").
_CHANGE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:add|adding|plus|more|double|triple|twice|half|chang\w+|revis\w+|updat\w+|instead|replac\w+|remov\w+|drop"
    r"|delet\w+|cancel\w*|except|less|fewer|extra|another|additional|increas\w+|decreas\w+|reduc\w+|correct\w*"
    r"|wrong|different|new|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve|dozen|couple|few|several)\b",
    re.I,
)


def body_text(email: dict) -> str:
    """The body as text. The HTML part keeps tables and the place of each pasted picture;
    plain text is the fallback, also when the HTML part is an empty shell."""
    return (html_to_text(email["html"]) if email.get("html") else "") or (email.get("text") or "")


def fingerprint(email: dict) -> dict:
    """The facts about one email that decide whether another email repeats it."""
    headers = email["headers"]
    subject = headers.get("subject") or ""
    lines = []
    for part in preparse(body_text(email), subject):
        if part["kind"] != "quoted":  # history under a reply is not part of what is being asked
            lines += [" ".join(line.lower().split()) for line in part["text"].splitlines() if line.strip()]
    try:
        sent = parsedate_to_datetime(headers.get("date") or "").timestamp()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        sent = None
    hashes = [a.get("sha256") for a in email["attachments"]]
    return {
        "sender": parseaddr(headers.get("from") or "")[1].lower(),
        "sent": sent,
        "message_id": (headers.get("message_id") or "").strip() or None,
        # None when a file's bytes were not available: then attachments cannot be compared.
        "attachments": None if None in hashes else frozenset(hashes),
        "has_file": any(not a.get("inline") for a in email["attachments"]),
        "lines": frozenset(lines),
        "number_lines": frozenset(line for line in lines if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in line)),
        "says_resend": bool(_RESEND.search(subject) or any(_RESEND.search(line) for line in lines)),
    }


def find_duplicates(emails: dict[str, dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {duplicate email id: original email id} for an inbox of parsed emails.

    The email with the later Date is the duplicate. A wrong "duplicate" would empty a real
    order, so every rule below needs positive evidence, and doubt means "not a duplicate".
    """
    prints = {eid: fingerprint(email) for eid, email in emails.items() if not email.get("error")}
    # Oldest first; emails with no usable date go last, in id order.
    order = sorted(prints, key=lambda eid: (prints[eid]["sent"] is None, prints[eid]["sent"] or 0, eid))
    duplicates: dict[str, str] = {}
    originals: list[str] = []
    for eid in order:
        match = next((o for o in originals if _same_request(prints[o], prints[eid])), None)
        if match:
            duplicates[eid] = match
        else:
            originals.append(eid)
    return duplicates


def _same_request(first: dict, later: dict) -> bool:
    if first["message_id"] and first["message_id"] == later["message_id"]:
        return True  # the very same email, delivered twice
    if first["sent"] is None or later["sent"] is None:
        return False  # cannot tell which one came later
    if not first["sender"] or first["sender"] != later["sender"]:
        return False
    if first["attachments"] is None or first["attachments"] != later["attachments"]:
        return False
    # Every line that carries a number (sizes, quantities, dates) must be the same in both.
    if first["number_lines"] != later["number_lines"]:
        return False
    # The words only the later email has must not ask for a change.
    if any(_CHANGE.search(line) for line in later["lines"] - first["lines"]):
        return False
    # Evidence that it is a repeat: the same attached file, the same text line for line,
    # or the later email saying so.
    return (first["has_file"] and later["has_file"]) or first["lines"] == later["lines"] or later["says_resend"]

"""MIME layer: turn .eml files into plain dicts, using data/eml_to_json.py.

This layer unpacks the email and hands each attachment to an AttachmentExtractor.
It does not decide anything about the email's meaning.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from data.eml_to_json import eml_to_json

from .attachments import AttachmentExtractor, unreadable


class MimeParser:
    """Parse every .eml in a directory. One bad email never stops the others."""

    def __init__(self, files_dir: Path | None = None, extractor: AttachmentExtractor | None = None):
        # Attachment bytes are written under files_dir/<email id>/<filename>.
        # With no files_dir, a temporary directory is used and removed afterwards.
        self.extractor = extractor
        self._temp_dir = None
        if files_dir is None:
            self._temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rfq_attachments_")
            files_dir = self._temp_dir.name
        self.files_dir = Path(files_dir)

    def parse_file(self, path: Path) -> dict:
        """Return one email as a dict. `error` is None unless the email could not be read.

        Each attachment gains `sha256` (a hash of its bytes, used to spot the same file sent
        twice) and, with an extractor, an `extraction` dict (see attachments/extractor.py).
        """
        path = Path(path)
        try:
            email = {**eml_to_json(path, self.files_dir), "error": None}
        except Exception as exc:  # a broken .eml is recorded, not raised
            return {
                "id": path.stem,
                "headers": {},
                "text": None,
                "html": None,
                "attachments": [],
                "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
            }
        for attachment in email["attachments"]:
            try:
                data = Path(attachment["path"]).read_bytes()
            except OSError as exc:
                data = None
                problem = f"attachment bytes could not be read ({type(exc).__name__})"
            attachment["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() if data is not None else None
            if self.extractor is not None:
                attachment["extraction"] = (
                    unreadable(attachment["filename"], problem)
                    if data is None
                    else self.extractor.extract(
                        label=email["id"], filename=attachment["filename"], mime=attachment["mime"], data=data
                    )
                )
        return email

    def parse_dir(self, emails_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
        """Return every .eml in the directory, keyed by filename stem, in name order."""
        return {p.stem: self.parse_file(p) for p in sorted(Path(emails_dir).glob("*.eml"))}

"""Pre-parser: split an email body into labelled parts before the model reads it.

Parts come back in the order they appear in the body, each with a kind:

    current    what the sender wrote in this message
    quoted     an earlier message quoted below (or inside) a reply
    forwarded  a message that is being passed on

Nothing is dropped: every body line lands in exactly one part. The labels are facts read
from quote marks and header lines. What a part means for the request is the model's call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

# "> text", "> > text": one mark per level of quoting.
_QUOTE_MARKS = re.compile(r"^((?:>\s?)+)")
# "-----Original Message-----", "---------- Forwarded message ---------", "Begin forwarded message:"
_SEPARATOR = re.compile(r"^\s*(-{2,}\s*(original message|forwarded message)\s*-{2,}|begin forwarded message:)\s*$", re.I)
# A header line as mail programs print it above a quoted message: "From: ...", "*Sent:* ..."
_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\*?(from|sent|date|to|cc|subject)\*?:\s*\S", re.I)
_FORWARD_SUBJECT = re.compile(r"^\s*(fw|fwd)\s*:", re.I)


def preparse(body: str, subject: str = "") -> list[dict]:
    """Return the body as a list of {"kind", "intro", "text"} parts.

    `intro` holds the lines that introduce an earlier message ("On ... wrote:", or a
    "From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:" block), or None.
    """
    lines = [_unquote(line) for line in body.splitlines()]
    forward_subject = bool(_FORWARD_SUBJECT.match(subject or ""))
    parts: list[dict] = []
    part = _open(parts, "current", 0)
    base_kind = "current"  # what unquoted text belongs to; changes after an unquoted header block
    first_boundary = True
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        depth, text = lines[i]
        if not text.strip():
            part["lines"].append("")
            i += 1
            continue

        # 1. A separator line or a header block starts an earlier message that runs on from here.
        separator = _SEPARATOR.match(text)
        header_lines = _header_block(lines, i, depth) if not separator else 0
        if separator or header_lines:
            start = i
            if separator:
                i += 1
                while i < len(lines) and not lines[i][1].strip():
                    i += 1
                header_lines = _header_run(lines, i, depth)
            i += header_lines
            explicit_forward = bool(separator) and "forward" in text.lower()
            kind = "forwarded" if explicit_forward or (first_boundary and forward_subject) else "quoted"
            intro = "\n".join(t for _, t in lines[start:i] if t.strip())
            part = _open(parts, kind, depth, intro)
            if depth == 0:
                base_kind = kind
            first_boundary = False
            continue

        # 2. "On <date> <name> wrote:" introduces the quoted lines that follow it.
        attribution = _attribution(lines, i, depth)
        if attribution:
            intro = " ".join(t.strip() for _, t in lines[i : i + attribution])
            part = _open(parts, "quoted", depth + 1, intro)
            first_boundary = False
            i += attribution
            continue

        # 3. A change in quote depth starts a new part: deeper is an older message,
        #    back to no marks is the surrounding message again.
        if depth != part["depth"]:
            part = _open(parts, base_kind if depth == 0 else "quoted", depth)
        part["lines"].append(text)
        i += 1

    out = []
    for part in parts:
        text = "\n".join(part["lines"]).strip("\n")
        if text.strip() or part["intro"]:
            out.append({"kind": part["kind"], "intro": part["intro"], "text": text})
    return out


def _open(parts: list[dict], kind: str, depth: int, intro: str | None = None) -> dict:
    part = {"kind": kind, "depth": depth, "intro": intro, "lines": []}
    parts.append(part)
    return part


def _unquote(line: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Return (quote depth, the line without its quote marks)."""
    marks = _QUOTE_MARKS.match(line)
    if not marks:
        return 0, line
    return marks.group(1).count(">"), line[marks.end() :]


def _header_run(lines: list, start: int, depth: int) -> int:
    """How many header lines ("From: ...", "Subject: ...") run on from `start` at this depth."""
    count = 0
    while start + count < len(lines):
        line_depth, text = lines[start + count]
        if line_depth != depth or not _HEADER.match(text):
            break
        count += 1
    return count


def _header_block(lines: list, start: int, depth: int) -> int:
    """Length of a header block that opens an earlier message here, or 0.

    It must start with From: and also carry a date line and a To: or Subject: line, so that
    one stray "From: the Houston yard" in a message is not taken for a boundary.
    """
    if not lines[start][1].lower().lstrip("*").startswith("from"):
        return 0
    count = _header_run(lines, start, depth)
    names = {_HEADER.match(text).group(1).lower() for _, text in lines[start : start + count]}
    if count >= 3 and names & {"sent", "date"} and names & {"to", "subject"}:
        return count
    return 0


def _attribution(lines: list, start: int, depth: int) -> int:
    """Number of lines (1 or 2) of an "On ... wrote:" line that introduces quoted text, or 0."""
    text = lines[start][1].strip()
    if not text.startswith("On "):
        return 0
    length = 0
    if text.endswith("wrote:"):
        length = 1
    elif start + 1 < len(lines) and lines[start + 1][0] == depth and lines[start + 1][1].strip().endswith("wrote:"):
        length = 2  # mail programs wrap this line when the address is long
    if not length:
        return 0
    following = next(((d, t) for d, t in lines[start + length :] if t.strip()), None)
    # Only a real introduction is followed by quoted lines; "On Monday we wrote: ..." is not.
    return length if following and following[0] > depth else 0

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile

class MimeParser:
    """Parse every .eml in a directory. One bad email never stops the others."""

    def __init__(self, files_dir: Path | None = None, extractor: AttachmentExtractor | None = None):
        # Attachment bytes are written under files_dir/<email id>/<filename>.
        # With no files_dir, a temporary directory is used and removed afterwards.
        self.extractor = extractor
        self._temp_dir = None
        if files_dir is None:
            self._temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rfq_attachments_")
            files_dir = self._temp_dir.name
        self.files_dir = Path(files_dir)

    def parse_file(self, path: Path) -> dict:
        """Return one email as a dict. `error` is None unless the email could not be read.

        Each attachment gains `sha256` (a hash of its bytes, used to spot the same file sent
        twice) and, with an extractor, an `extraction` dict (see attachments/extractor.py).
